mainTopic: The ברייתא that reads the זקן ממרא פסוק word by word, the three opinions on what kind of law makes a זקן ממרא liable, and רב פפא's explanation of the ברייתא according to רבי מאיר.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about the זקן ממרא (דברים 17:8) one word at a time. The ברייתא says the פסוק is about the top judge of a court, a מופלא who is also a יועץ, an adviser. Each word stands for an area of תורה: הלכה and דין, kinds of blood, court cases and נגעים, vows and dedications, special rituals, and gifts to the poor. Then it teaches that the judges go up to the בית דין הגדול, and that the chosen place is what gives its ruling force. The גמרא finds a source in ירמיהו for the idea that ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands. Next comes a new ברייתא with three opinions on what kind of law makes a זקן ממרא liable. רבי מאיר requires כרת and חטאת, רבי יהודה requires a Torah root with a Rabbinic explanation, and רבי שמעון includes even a tiny detail, and the גמרא gives each one's source. Finally, רב פפא explains the first ברייתא according to רבי מאיר, showing how calendar rulings and the הלכה of the eleven days can lead to sins with כרת. His explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse is about the top judge of the court
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the פסוק of זקן ממרא is talking about the מופלא, the most distinguished judge of a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse is speaking about the most outstanding member of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us who the פסוק is about: not just any person, but the greatest expert judge of a court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק opens with 'כי יפלא', meaning 'if a matter is too hard for you.' The ברייתא reads this word as a hint to the מופלא, the outstanding judge. So the whole law of זקן ממרא only applies to a top-level, qualified judge, not to an ordinary person.

keyTerms.meaning: The most distinguished, expert judge of a court
A Jewish court
The verse is speaking (about this case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the boundaries of the whole דין of זקן ממרא: only someone of this level can become a rebellious elder.

phrases.english: About the most distinguished member of the court
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is reading the פסוק 'כי יפלא ממך דבר' (דברים 17:8). The word יפלא sounds like מופלא.

phrases.english: the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law of the זקן ממרא applies to the מופלא, the outstanding judge of the court.

steps.title: The word 'from you' means an adviser
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads 'ממך' as referring to a יועץ, an adviser.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From you': this refers to an adviser.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next word of the פסוק, ממך, and says it points to a judge who also serves as an adviser.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds another quality of the judge in question: he is someone people come to for advice. In the next step the ברייתא brings a פסוק to show that the word ממך is linked to the idea of an adviser.

keyTerms.meaning: From you
An adviser, someone consulted on important matters

phrases.english: 'From you': this is an adviser,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second quality of the judge after מופלא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ממך teaches that the judge is a יועץ.

steps.title: A verse in נחום links 'from you' with an adviser
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves that ממך means an adviser from a פסוק in נחום, where the same word appears right next to 'adviser'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it says: 'From you came out one who plans evil against ה׳, an adviser of wickedness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא backs up its reading of ממך with a פסוק where ממך and יועץ appear together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In נחום the word ממך is followed directly by 'יעץ בליעל', an adviser of wickedness. Because the two words go together there, the ברייתא reads ממך in our פסוק as pointing to an adviser too. The proof is about the word connection, not about the wicked content.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says (introduces a supporting פסוק)
An adviser of wickedness

phrases.english: and likewise it says:
'From you came out one who plans evil against ה׳,'
'an adviser of wickedness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The reading of ממך as יועץ.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נחום 1:11, where ממך appears right next to יועץ.

steps.title: 'A matter' is הלכה and 'for judgment' is דין
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads דבר as הלכה and למשפט as דין, the two main ways laws are known.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A matter': this is a הלכה. 'For judgment': this is a דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains two more words of the פסוק. Each one stands for a kind of legal question the elder might argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דבר refers to a law known through tradition (הלכה). למשפט refers to a law reached by reasoning and learning out from פסוקים (דין). So the disagreement can be about something received by tradition or about something worked out by logic.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter (here read as הלכה)
A law known by tradition
For judgment
Here, a law reached through reasoning

phrases.english: 'A matter': this is a halacha.
phrases.notes: Here הלכה means a law that was handed down, not worked out by reasoning.

phrases.english: 'For judgment': this is the logical inference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from describing the judge to describing the kinds of questions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute can be about a הלכה or about a דין.

steps.title: Three kinds of blood, judgments and marks
steps.stepSummary: Each pair in the פסוק (blood and blood, judgment and judgment, mark and mark) stands for three related areas of law that the judge must tell apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Between blood and blood': between the blood of a נדה, the blood of birth, and the blood of a זבה. 'Between judgment and judgment': between capital cases, money cases and cases of lashes. 'Between mark and mark': between צרעת marks on a person, on houses and on clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains three phrases in the פסוק. Each one names a group of laws that look similar but have different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of 'between X and X' is telling apart similar cases. Blood covers נדה, לידה and זיבה. Judgment covers capital cases, money cases and lashes. Marks covers נגעים of a person, a house and a garment. A disagreement in any of these areas can make someone a זקן ממרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of a menstruating woman
Blood after giving birth
Blood of a זבה (an irregular flow)
Capital cases
Money cases
צרעת marks on houses

phrases.english: 'Between blood and blood':

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין דַּם נִדָּה, דַּם לֵידָה, דַּם זִיבָה.
phrases.english: between the blood of a niddah, blood of childbirth, and blood of ziva.
'Between plea and plea':

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת, דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת, דִּינֵי מַכּוֹת.
phrases.english: between capital cases, monetary cases, and cases of lashes.
'Between mark and mark':

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין נִגְעֵי אָדָם, נִגְעֵי בָתִּים, נִגְעֵי בְגָדִים.
phrases.english: between leprous marks of a person, marks on houses, and marks on garments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the פסוק word by word, now with three subject areas.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק covers the laws of blood, kinds of court cases, and kinds of נגעים.

steps.title: Matters of speech, controversy, and gifts to the poor
steps.stepSummary: דברי refers to חרמים, ערכין and הקדשות. ריבת refers to סוטה, עגלה ערופה and טהרת מצורע. בשעריך refers to לקט, שכחה and פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Matters of': these are חרמים, ערכין and הקדשות. 'Controversy': this is giving the water to a סוטה, breaking the neck of the עגלה, and purifying a מצורע. 'In your gates': this is לקט, שכחה and פאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes going through the words of the פסוק, and each word again stands for a group of three laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דברי, meaning 'words', fits laws that come about through speaking: dedications, valuations and consecrations. ריבת, meaning 'controversy', fits rituals connected to a fight or problem. בשעריך, meaning 'in your gates', fits gifts given to the poor in the city. This widens the range of topics where the elder's disagreement counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Items dedicated by a חרם vow
Pledges of a person's fixed value to the מקדש
Giving the bitter water to a סוטה
Breaking the neck of the calf for an unsolved murder
Gleanings, forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field, all left for the poor

phrases.english: 'Matters of': these are the dedications,
and the valuations, and the consecrations.
'Controversy': this is giving the waters to a sota,
and the heifer whose neck is broken, and the purification of a leper.
'Within your gates': this is gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and pe'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of subject areas hinted to in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק also covers vows and dedications, the rituals of 'controversy', and gifts to the poor.

steps.title: Arising from court and going up to the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: וקמת means getting up from the local court, and ועלית teaches that the בית המקדש is higher than ארץ ישראל, which is higher than all other lands.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And you shall arise': from the court. 'And you shall go up': this teaches that the בית המקדש is higher than ארץ ישראל, and ארץ ישראל is higher than all the lands.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now moves to the second half of the פסוק, which describes the judges leaving their court and going up to the בית דין הגדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: וקמת tells us the judges get up from their local court to ask their question. The word ועלית, 'go up', teaches that the בית המקדש is higher than the rest of ארץ ישראל, and ארץ ישראל is higher than every other land. That is why the פסוק speaks of 'going up' to it.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall arise
And you shall go up
Teaches
The Temple

steps.confusionAlert: וקמת is not about standing up for respect. It means getting up and leaving your local court to go ask the בית דין הגדול.

phrases.english: 'Then you shall arise': from the court.
'And ascend': this teaches
that the Temple is higher than Eretz Yisrael,
and Eretz Yisrael is higher than all the lands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the subject areas to the process of going up to the בית דין הגדול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The judges leave their court and go up. The בית המקדש is higher than ארץ ישראל, which is higher than all lands.

steps.title: The place itself gives the ruling its power
steps.stepSummary: אל המקום teaches that the chosen place causes the ruling to count, so the זקן ממרא is only liable for going against a ruling given there.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To the place': this teaches that the place is what causes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by explaining 'אל המקום': the special place of the בית דין הגדול is what makes its ruling binding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not enough that great judges ruled. They must rule in the place ה׳ chose. Only then does going against their ruling make someone a זקן ממרא. This ties the whole reading back to the משנה's דין.

keyTerms.meaning: To the place (ה׳ will choose)
The place is what causes it (gives the ruling its force)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא reads every word of the פסוק. The זקן ממרא is a top judge, the dispute can be in almost any area of תורה, and the ruling counts because it was given in the chosen place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the law of זקן ממרא depends on the בית דין הגדול sitting in its proper place, and not just on who the judges are.

phrases.english: 'To the place': this teaches
that the place causes it.
phrases.notes: He means the chosen place is what makes the court's ruling binding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the description of going up to the בית דין הגדול by explaining why its location matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The chosen place is what gives the ruling its binding force.

steps.title: Where do we learn that ארץ ישראל is higher than other lands?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the בית המקדש being higher than ארץ ישראל comes from the word ועלית. It asks for the source that ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the בית המקדש is higher than ארץ ישראל, because it says 'and you shall go up.' But where does the ברייתא learn that ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from step 7 and asks for a source for its second claim. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ועלית only shows going up from the local court to the בית המקדש, which is inside ארץ ישראל. It says nothing about going from other countries to ארץ ישראל. So that second claim still needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense
Higher
From where does he know it?

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ גָּבוֹהַּ מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: Granted, the Temple is higher than the Land of Israel,
as it is written: "And you shall go up."

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל גָּבוֹהַּ מִכׇּל הָאֲרָצוֹת
phrases.english: But that the Land of Israel is higher than all the lands,
from where does he know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ גָּבוֹהַּ מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's claim in step 7 and asks for a missing source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands.

steps.title: A verse in ירמיהו calls coming to ארץ ישראל 'going up'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes ירמיהו, which says ה׳ 'brought up' the Jews from all the lands to their own land. This shows that ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says: 'Days are coming when people will no longer say, As ה׳ lives, Who brought up Israel from Egypt, but rather, As ה׳ lives, Who brought up and brought the descendants of Israel from the north and from all the lands where I scattered them, and they will live on their land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a פסוק. In that פסוק, coming back to ארץ ישראל from every land is called 'bringing up.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is הֶעֱלָה, 'brought up,' used for the return from all the lands of exile. If coming into ארץ ישראל from anywhere is called going up, then ארץ ישראל is 'higher' than every other land.

keyTerms.meaning: He brought up
I scattered them
The northern land

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״לָכֵן הִנֵּה יָמִים בָּאִים נְאֻם ה׳
phrases.english: As it is written: "Therefore, behold, days are coming, says ה׳,
when it will no longer be said: As ה׳ lives,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר הֶעֱלָה אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם.
phrases.english: Who brought up the children of Israel from the land of Egypt.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִם חַי ה׳ אֲשֶׁר הֶעֱלָה
phrases.english: Rather: As ה׳ lives, Who brought up

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲשֶׁר הֵבִיא אֶת זֶרַע בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: and Who brought the descendants of the house of Israel
from the northern land and from all the lands

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר הִדַּחְתִּים שָׁם וְיָשְׁבוּ עַל אַדְמָתָם״.
phrases.english: where I had scattered them, and they will live on their land."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: לָכֵן הִנֵּה יָמִים בָּאִים נְאֻם ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ירמיהו describes the return from all the lands to ארץ ישראל as 'bringing up,' so ארץ ישראל is higher than all lands.
steps.whatToRemember: The בית המקדש is higher than ארץ ישראל because of ועלית. ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands because ירמיהו calls coming there from all the lands הֶעֱלָה, 'brought up.'

steps.title: Three opinions on which kind of law makes a rebellious elder liable
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings three opinions. רבי מאיר: only a law punished by כרת if done on purpose and by a חטאת if done by mistake. רבי יהודה: a law whose core is in the Torah but whose explanation comes from the Rabbis. רבי שמעון: even one small detail of the Rabbis.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A זקן ממרא is liable only for a matter that brings כרת if done on purpose and a חטאת if done by mistake. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: for a matter whose core is from the Torah and whose explanation is from the Rabbis. רבי שמעון says: even for one small detail of the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It asks how serious a law must be for a זקן ממרא to be liable for ruling against the Great Court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three opinions go from strictest limit to widest. רבי מאיר limits it to very serious laws, those with כרת and חטאת. רבי יהודה requires a Torah root with a Rabbinic explanation, and רבי שמעון includes even one small Rabbinic detail.

keyTerms.meaning: A rebellious elder, a scholar who rules against the Great Court
If done on purpose the punishment is כרת, if done by mistake one brings a sin-offering
Its core comes from the Torah
The words of the Rabbis (literally, the scribes)
A fine detail

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying any Rabbinic law counts. The law needs both parts: a root written in the Torah and an explanation that comes from the Rabbis.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: זָקֵן מַמְרֵא אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר
phrases.english: A rebellious elder is liable only for a matter
whose intentional violation brings כרת and whose accidental violation brings a sin-offering,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says: for a matter
whose core is from the words of the Torah
and whose explanation is from the words of the scribes.
Rabbi Shimon says:
Even one fine detail of the fine details of the scribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: זָקֵן מַמְרֵא אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the ruling must be given to what kind of law the ruling must be about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three views on what kind of law makes a זקן ממרא liable: כרת and חטאת (רבי מאיר), a Torah root with a Rabbinic explanation (רבי יהודה), or even a small Rabbinic detail (רבי שמעון).
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets the frame for the rest of the sugya, which explains the reason behind each opinion.

steps.title: Asking for רבי מאיר's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source רבי מאיר uses to limit liability to laws with כרת and חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי מאיר's opinion. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים about the זקן ממרא do not say anything about כרת or חטאת. So the גמרא wants to know where רבי מאיר gets this limit.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי מאיר's limit of כרת and חטאת.

steps.title: רבי מאיר learns 'matter' from 'matter'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר makes a גזירה שוה between the word דבר in the זקן ממרא section and the word דבר in the section about the congregation's sin-offering. That offering is only brought for a sin with כרת and חטאת, so the same limit applies to the זקן ממרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'matter' from 'matter.' Here it says, 'If a matter is too hard for you in judgment,' and there it says, 'And a matter is hidden from the eyes of the congregation.' Just as there it is a matter that brings כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake, so too here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר uses a גזירה שוה, linking two פסוקים through the same word, דבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא, the congregation brings a special sin-offering when the court made a mistake. That only applies to a sin that carries כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake. Since both sections use the word דבר, רבי מאיר applies the same limit to the זקן ממרא.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (one thing from another)
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places
Here / there
Just as there, so too here

phrases.english: He learns "matter" from "matter."

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״כִּי יִפָּלֵא מִמְּךָ דָבָר לַמִּשְׁפָּט״,
phrases.english: It is written here: "If a matter is too hard for you in judgment,"
and it is written there: "And a matter is hidden from the eyes of the congregation."
Just as there, it is a matter

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁחַיָּיב עַל זְדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת וְעַל שִׁגְגָתוֹ חַטָּאת,
phrases.english: for whose intentional violation one is liable to כרת and for whose accidental violation to a sin-offering,
so too here, it is a matter

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁחַיָּיב עַל זְדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת וְעַל שִׁגְגָתוֹ חַטָּאת.
phrases.english: for whose intentional violation one is liable to כרת and for whose accidental violation to a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word דבר links the זקן ממרא to the congregation's sin-offering, which is limited to sins with כרת and חטאת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's reason: both 'Torah' and 'they will teach you'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק 'according to the Torah that they will teach you.' A זקן ממרא is liable only when the law has both parts: a Torah root and the Rabbis' teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? It says, 'According to the Torah that they will teach you,' so he is not liable until there is both 'Torah' and 'they will teach you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבי יהודה's source. It is a פסוק that mentions both the Torah and the teaching of the judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תורה points to the written root of the law. The word יורוך, 'they will teach you,' points to the explanation the Rabbis give. Only when both are present is the זקן ממרא liable, which matches רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: They will teach you (the judges' explanation)
Not until there is

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the words 'what is his reason,' but that is the question.

phrases.english: "According to the Torah that they will teach you"
He is not liable until there is both "Torah" and "they will teach you."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the pattern of step 12 and gives the reason for the second opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק needs both תורה (a written root) and יורוך (a Rabbinic explanation) for the זקן ממרא to be liable.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר uses a גזירה שוה on דבר to require כרת and חטאת. רבי יהודה uses 'התורה אשר יורוך' to require a Torah root plus a Rabbinic explanation.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's source: even a tiny detail
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from the words 'from that place' that a זקן ממרא is liable for disagreeing on even the smallest detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון learns his view from the פסוק 'that they will tell you from that place.' This teaches that he is liable even for any small detail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the third opinion, רבי שמעון's. This completes the list of sources for the three opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר needed a גזירה שוה, and רבי יהודה needed a law with both a Torah root and the Rabbis' explanation. רבי שמעון reads 'whatever they tell you from that place' with no limit at all. So any ruling of the great בית דין, even a small rabbinic detail, counts.

keyTerms.meaning: any amount at all, even something tiny
'that place', the seat of the great בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on how big the law must be: רבי מאיר says only laws with כרת and חטאת. רבי יהודה says a Torah root plus the Rabbis' explanation. רבי שמעון says even a tiny detail.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon (what is his source?):
"That they will tell you from that place"
even anything at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and last source, following רבי יהודה's source in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'that they will tell you from that place' has no limit, so even a small detail counts.

steps.title: Explain the ברייתא according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא asks רבא to explain the ברייתא according to רבי מאיר, and רבא sends רב פפא to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא said to רבא: Explain this ברייתא for me according to רבי מאיר. רבא said to רב פפא: Go explain it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. If רבי מאיר is right that only laws with כרת and חטאת count, how does each item in the ברייתא fit? This sets up רב פפא's explanation in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists many kinds of rulings learned from each word of the פסוק. Some of them, like the יועץ or gifts to the poor (לקט, שכחה and פאה), do not look like laws with כרת and חטאת. So רב הונא wants to see how each one can lead to a sin with כרת according to רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: explain it to me
according to the view of
go

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana said to Rava:
Explain this teaching for me
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that goes through the זקן ממרא פסוק word by word, starting with 'כי יפלא'.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Meir.
Rava said to Rav Pappa:
Go explain it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ לִי לְהָא מַתְנִיתָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the sources are done, the גמרא tests רבי מאיר's limit against the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How each ruling in the ברייתא can involve a law with כרת and חטאת, as רבי מאיר requires.

steps.title: The adviser who sets the calendar
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that 'כי יפלא' is about the top judge, and 'ממך' is about the adviser who knows how to make leap years and set months. He cites a משנה about adding a month during אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If it is too hard' means the פסוק is talking about the greatest judge in the court. 'For you' means the adviser, who knows how to make leap years and set the months. As we learned in a משנה: They testified that a leap year may be declared during all of אדר, because the others used to say only until פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא starts explaining the ברייתא word by word. 'ממך' refers to calendar rulings, and he shows that the Sages really did argue about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was how a calendar ruling could ever carry כרת. Here רב פפא first shows that the calendar is a real area where Sages disagree. One opinion lets the court add a month during all of אדר, and another only until פורים. The next step shows why such a disagreement leads to a sin with כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: the most outstanding judge of the court
adviser, an expert in the calendar
to make a year into a leap year by adding a month
to set when each month begins
as we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: 'כי יפלא' here does not mean 'too hard' in the usual sense. The ברייתא reads it as 'מופלא', the outstanding judge, to tell us who the זקן ממרא is.

phrases.english: "If it is too hard"
the verse is speaking about the most outstanding judge of the court.
"For you": this is the adviser,
who knows how to make leap years and set the months.
As we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵעִידוּ שֶׁמְּעַבְּרִים אֶת הַשָּׁנָה כׇּל אֲדָר,
phrases.english: They testified that the year may be made a leap year during all of Adar,
phrases.notes: 'They' are earlier Sages whose testimony is recorded in a משנה.

phrases.english: because others used to say only until Purim.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״מִמְּךָ״ – זֶה יוֹעֵץ, שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לְעַבֵּר שָׁנִים וְלִקְבּוֹעַ חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב פפא begins answering the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ממך' covers calendar rulings, which really are argued about, as the dispute over 'all of אדר' versus 'until פורים' shows.

steps.title: Either way, he permits חמץ on פסח
steps.stepSummary: A wrong calendar ruling in either direction leads people to eat חמץ on the real פסח, which carries כרת and חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if he rules one way, he permits חמץ on פסח. And if he rules the other way, he also permits חמץ on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his point. Arguing with the court about the leap year leads to a sin with כרת, so it fits רבי מאיר's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the court added a month and the elder says it did not. Then he puts פסח a month too early, and on the real פסח people will eat חמץ. Suppose instead the court did not add a month and the elder says it did. Then he puts פסח a month too late, so on the real פסח people will eat חמץ. Eating חמץ on פסח carries כרת if done on purpose and a חטאת if done by mistake, so it meets רבי מאיר's test.

keyTerms.meaning: to this side, in one direction
permits
leavened food on פסח, a sin with כרת

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, a calendar ruling counts for a זקן ממרא because a mistake in either direction lets people eat חמץ on the real פסח.
steps.confusionAlert: The two halves use the same words but mean opposite directions. The first is 'no leap year when there is one', and the second is 'a leap year when there is none'. Both end with eating חמץ on the true פסח.

phrases.english: For if he rules to this side,
phrases.notes: For example, the court made a leap year and he says it is not one, so his פסח comes a month too early.

phrases.english: he permits leavened food on Passover.
And if he rules to the other side,
phrases.notes: For example, the court made no leap year and he says it is one, so his פסח comes a month too late.

phrases.english: he permits leavened food on Passover.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לְהַאי גִּיסָא, קָא שָׁרֵי חָמֵץ בְּפֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 17 by showing why a calendar disagreement carries כרת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A wrong calendar ruling in either direction permits חמץ on the real פסח, which carries כרת and חטאת, so it fits רבי מאיר.

steps.title: The word 'a matter' means a הלכה: the eleven days
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the word 'דבר' in the פסוק refers to a הלכה, specifically the הלכה of the eleven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A matter' means a הלכה. This is the הלכה of the eleven days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא moves to the next word in the פסוק, 'דבר', and says it refers to a הלכה. His example is the eleven days between one נדה period and the next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the פסוק points to a different kind of law where a זקן ממרא could become liable. 'דבר' covers a הלכה, a law passed down rather than learned from a פסוק. The eleven days of זיבה is such a הלכה, and a mistake about it can lead to a כרת issue.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A matter'. A word from the פסוק about a זקן ממרא.
A law handed down by tradition, not learned from a פסוק.
The eleven days after a woman's נדה week, when blood can make her a זבה.

phrases.english: 'A matter': this is a הלכה.
phrases.notes: 'דבר' is a word from the פסוק 'כי יפלא ממך דבר למשפט' (דברים 17:8).

phrases.english: This is the הלכה of the eleven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב פפא's word-by-word reading of the פסוק, after 'כי יפלא' and 'ממך' (steps 17-18).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'דבר' refers to a הלכה, such as the eleven days of זיבה.

steps.title: The argument about blood on the tenth day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a מחלוקת: רבי יוחנן says the tenth day is like the ninth, and ריש לקיש says it is like the eleventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: about the tenth day, רבי יוחנן says the tenth is like the ninth, and רבי שמעון בן לקיש says the tenth is like the eleventh.
steps.whatsHappening: To show how a real כרת argument can come up in the eleven days, the גמרא brings an argument about a woman who sees blood on the tenth day. This step only states the two opinions. The next steps explain them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This argument is the example of a הלכה matter where courts could disagree. One opinion treats the tenth day like the days before it, and the other treats it like the last day. Because the two views lead to different rulings about her status, a ruling either way could involve כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it was stated'. Introduces a quoted argument between אמוראים.
The tenth day of the eleven days.
The ninth day.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Tenth' and 'ninth' do not mean days of the month. They are days counted inside the eleven-day stretch after her נדה week.

phrases.english: As it was stated: about the tenth day,
phrases.notes: He means a woman who saw blood on the tenth of the eleven days.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: the tenth is like the ninth,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: עֲשִׂירִי כְּאַחַד עָשָׂר.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: the tenth is like the eleventh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a real argument inside the 'הלכת אחד עשר' named in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the tenth day is like the ninth. ריש לקיש: the tenth day is like the eleventh.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reasoning: the tenth needs a guarded day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that, just like the ninth day, blood on the tenth day requires her to guard the next day as clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said the tenth is like the ninth: just as the ninth requires guarding, the tenth also requires guarding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out רבי יוחנן's view. Blood on the tenth day means she must watch the next day, the eleventh, to see that it stays clean, just as she would after blood on the ninth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After blood on the ninth day, the next day is still inside the eleven days, so she must guard it. רבי יוחנן says the same about the tenth day, even though the day she guards is the eleventh, the last of the eleven days. So in his view she must keep the eleventh day clean before she can go to the מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires, needs.
Guarding: watching a day to see that it stays free of blood.
'Just as... so too...'. A comparison.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said the tenth is like the ninth:
just as the ninth requires guarding,
phrases.notes: Guarding means she has to watch the next day and make sure it is clean before she can go to the מקוה.

phrases.english: so too the tenth requires guarding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first opinion in the argument from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood on the tenth day requires guarding the eleventh day, just like blood on the ninth day.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's reasoning: the tenth needs no guarded day
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that, just like the eleventh day, blood on the tenth day does not require her to guard the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said the tenth is like the eleventh: just as the eleventh does not require guarding, the tenth also does not require guarding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out ריש לקיש's view. Blood on the tenth day does not require her to guard the eleventh day, just as blood on the eleventh day does not require guarding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood on the eleventh day needs no guarded day, because the next day is already past the eleven days. ריש לקיש puts the tenth day in that same group. So the two opinions disagree on whether the eleventh day still needs guarding, and that changes the woman's status.

keyTerms.meaning: Short name for רבי שמעון בן לקיש.
Does not require.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: blood on day ten requires guarding day eleven. ריש לקיש: it does not. Because the two views lead to different rulings, a court and a זקן ממרא could argue here on a matter of כרת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even a law that comes from tradition (a הלכה) can have real arguments in its details. That is what makes it count as a 'דבר' where a זקן ממרא can be liable.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר, עֲשִׂירִי כְּאַחַד עָשָׂר:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said the tenth is like the eleventh:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אַחַד עָשָׂר לֹא בָּעֵי שִׁימּוּר –
phrases.english: just as the eleventh does not require guarding,
so too the tenth does not require guarding.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר, עֲשִׂירִי כְּאַחַד עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second opinion, set against רבי יוחנן's reasoning in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood on the tenth day does not require guarding the eleventh day, just like blood on the eleventh day.

steps.title: The word 'judgment' means a דין
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא moves to the next word in the פסוק: 'משפט' refers to a דין, a law learned through reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Judgment': this is a דין, a law learned through reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא moves to the next word in the פסוק, 'משפט', and says it refers to a דין. This step opens a new example, and the גמרא explains it on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After 'דבר' covered a הלכה, 'משפט' covers a law the Rabbis work out through reasoning. The point is that a זקן ממרא can be liable for arguing on that kind of law too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Judgment'. The next word in the פסוק.
Here, a law worked out through reasoning, such as a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: 'Judgment': this is a logical derivation.
phrases.notes: 'משפט' is the next word in the same פסוק, 'דבר למשפט' (דברים 17:8).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the word-by-word reading after finishing the example for 'דבר' in steps 19-22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'משפט' refers to a דין, a law learned through reasoning.
